To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the t -YSZ phase is present in the YSZ electrolyte and anode of commercial cells and the t -YS2 domains are enlarged in the anode upon cell operation.
the YSZ in SOFC cells has a nanoscale tetragonal domain that is randomly oriented in the cubic domain matrix and is unchanged after cell operating.
the YSZ in an SOFC is not pure c-YSZ but contains t-YSZ domains with sizes ranging from 2 to 10 nm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the crystallographic defects and microstructure of YSZ in commercial SOFC cells, which is critical to the long-term stability of YSZ and thus the performance of SOFCs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the YSZ crystal structure remains stable during cell operation, while t -YSZ domain formation occurs in the vicinity of the anode/electrolyte interface.
YSZ in SOFC cells is a composite of c -YSZ and t -YSZ.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
YSZ is not a single phase but rather a multiphase system, and that the crystal defects in YSZ can evolve with time and temperature.
the t -YSZ domain is formed in YSZ by the presence of oxygen vacancies and/or the existence of a high energy surface.
t -YSZ domain formation is not only related to the cell operation but also the fabrication process.

the YSZ crystallographic defects in the anode, cathode, and electrolyte can be identified and their evolution upon SOFC operation can be tracked by TEM.
